title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 97
paragraphs: When they straightway proposed the question whom they should set up to be king, Deioces was much put forward and commended by everyone, until at last they agreed that he should be their king. He bade them build for him a palace worthy of the royal dignity and strengthen him with a guard of spearmen. The Medes did so: they built him a large and strong palace in that part of the land which he indicated, and they allowed him to select spearmen from all the Medes. When he had obtained the rule over them, he compelled the Medes to make one fortified city and to pay chief attention to it, having less regard for the other cities. And as the Medes obeyed him in this also, he built large and strong walls—those which are now called Ecbatana—standing in circles one within the other. This wall is so contrived that one circle is higher than the next by the height of its battlements alone. To some extent, I suppose, the nature of the ground, since it is on a hill, assists toward this end; but much more was it produced by art, since the circles are seven in number altogether. Within the last circle are the royal palace and the treasure-houses. The largest of these walls is in size about equal to the circuit of the wall around Athens. And of the first circle the battlements are white, of the second black, of the third crimson, of the fourth blue, of the fifth red—thus the battlements of all the circles are colored with various tints; and the two innermost have their battlements, one of them overlaid with silver and the other with gold.
